headline: GOLD CRASHES TO $4,168 ON HOT MAY CPI: Fed Rate Hike Odds Hit 70%; $4,000 Is the Next Key Support
snippet: Gold fell to $4,168.50 — down $104 on the day — after the May 2026 CPI print hit 4.2% year-over-year, the highest reading since 2023, pushing December Fed rate-hike odds above 70% and erasing the metal's entire year-to-date gain for the first time since January. With the partial Iran-Israel ceasefire already unwinding the geopolitical premium and the blowout May jobs report (172K vs. 85K consensus) already repriced, Wednesday's CPI became the decisive binary event; a hot reading is now extending the sell-off toward $4,000 support, a level last tested in Q3 2025.

headline: ROCKY SHORE FINDS BULK GOLD ZONE AT APPLETON FAULT; Newfoundland Drill Budget Tripled to 12,500m After Discovery
snippet: Rocky Shore Gold Ltd. (CSE: RSG) reported June 10 that initial reconnaissance drilling at the Lane Pond Gold Target in central Newfoundland — along the prolific Appleton Fault Corridor — has intersected a near-surface bulk-style gold zone across 13 of 13 completed holes, warranting an immediate expansion from 3,500 to 12,500 metres. The Appleton Fault is the same structural corridor that hosts Newfoundland's best-known gold deposits; Rocky Shore's discovery opens both a broad bulk-tonnage system and structurally controlled higher-grade targets within the Gold Anchor Project.

headline: COPPER TARIFF CLOCK TICKING: Section 232 Ruling Due Mid-June; LME Slips to $13,567 as CPI and Iran Double Up
snippet: LME three-month copper fell 0.36% to $13,566.50 per tonne on June 10 as macro headwinds — the U.S.-Iran military exchange and a hot May CPI print — weighed against tariff-driven price support ahead of the Commerce Secretary's Section 232 recommendation, due before mid-June. Goldman Sachs has moved a 25% copper tariff to its base case; COMEX already carries a 6% premium over LME. The backdrop includes a forecast 600,000-tonne 2026 supply deficit (Morgan Stanley), delayed Grasberg restart, and Chilean output down 9% year-on-year.

headline: SILVER BARGAIN HUNTERS ARRIVE AT 2-MONTH LOW; Money Metals Identifies Physical Accumulation Zone Near 200-Day Average
snippet: Silver plunged almost 9% through a key price support level on June 8, touching its lowest close since late March, as paper-market liquidation overwhelmed industrial bid support — but a Money Metals Exchange analysis reports that retail demand for physical silver coins and small bars spiked sharply during the selloff. The firm's data identifies the current zone near the 200-day moving average as consistent with prior accumulation phases that historically resolved higher within 60 days, citing persistently elevated solar manufacturing demand and the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit as structural underpinnings.

headline: MINING.COM OP-ED: LITHIUM'S THREAT IS PRICING, NOT DEMAND — Sodium-Ion Batteries Target Battery Metals' Stationary Storage Heartland
snippet: A Mining.com opinion piece published June 9 argues that lithium's bull case faces a structural challenge demand forecasters consistently understate: sodium-ion batteries are gaining commercial traction specifically in stationary energy storage — the segment lithium bulls rely on for demand growth beyond EVs. With sodium-ion's cost advantage in applications where energy density matters less, including grid storage and industrial UPS systems, the author contends a meaningful fraction of the projected demand ramp could shift away from lithium, making the investment thesis more sensitive to EV adoption timing than the consensus currently assumes.

headline: QUESTCORP SPUDS MEXICO PHASE 2: La Union Gold-Silver Carbonate Replacement District Gets First Modern Drill Test in Sonora
snippet: Questcorp Mining Inc. (CSE: QQQ) commenced a fully funded ~1,500-metre, 8-to-10 hole Phase 2 diamond drill campaign on June 9 at the La Union Gold-Silver Project in Sonora, Mexico — the first modern, technology-driven drilling ever completed at a site that historically produced ~50,000 oz Au from high-grade oxide ore before the 1950s. The program targets untouched sulfide extensions and structural roots of a carbonate replacement system; 2026 field work returned high-grade gold, silver, lead and zinc from multiple target areas across the La Union, Union Norte, Javalí and Creston zones.

headline: CENTRAL BANKS BOUGHT NET 20 TONS GOLD IN MAY Despite Paper Selloff — GoldSeek SWOT: Sovereign Physical Floor Holds
snippet: The latest weekly Gold SWOT from US Global Investors (published via GoldSeek) notes that global central banks purchased a net 20 tonnes of gold in May 2026, maintaining structural accumulation pace despite the paper-market selloff driven by the U.S. jobs report and geopolitical ceasefire. The data highlights a growing disconnect between Western institutional paper selling and sovereign physical buying: the same month gold ETFs saw their first net-outflow month since early 2025, central banks collectively absorbed the equivalent of roughly two large mine operations' monthly output.

headline: RARE EARTH WAR EXPANDS INTO LAOS: China Secures 517 Mine Sites for Dysprosium and Terbium as Myanmar KIA Disrupts Supply Corridor
snippet: China has accelerated heavy rare earth extraction in Laos — satellite imagery identifies 517 suspected mining sites, with 23 of 27 formal mines opened since 2022 located inside protected areas — as Myanmar's Kachin Independence Army (KIA) continues to control the Chipwi and Pangwa mining hubs that previously supplied ~16% of global rare earth production. Dysprosium and terbium, essential for EV motor magnets and precision-guided weapons, are the primary targets; China processes ~98% of global supply of both. The KIA seizure in October 2024 drove a +20.7% terbium price surge in April 2026 alone, with Benchmark Mineral Intelligence forecasting China-Myanmar will still dominate 80% of global dysprosium/terbium supply through 2031.

headline: GOLDMAN, CHINA, CPI AND THE FED: Four Forces Pulling Gold in Opposite Directions — GoldSilver.com Explains the Disconnect
snippet: A GoldSilver.com analysis published June 10 maps the four competing forces creating gold's most complex market environment of 2026: Goldman Sachs simultaneously abandoning its rate-cut forecast while maintaining a $5,400 year-end gold target; China's physical accumulation program absorbing what Western ETFs are selling; the May CPI forcing a hawkish macro recalibration; and a Federal Reserve now more likely to hike than cut by December. The piece argues that investors conflating rate expectations with gold's structural demand drivers are misreading the setup — and that $4,168 represents a rare misalignment between paper sentiment and fundamental positioning.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER ALL MISPRICED — 'We're Bullish' as Paper Liquidation Overshoots Physical Reality
snippet: A GoldSeek multi-metals update argues that the synchronized selloff across gold, silver and copper from macro-driven paper liquidation has created mispriced floors across all three: gold near $4,168 with central bank buying structurally intact, silver at two-month lows building a physical accumulation base, and copper weighed down by rate-hike fears despite a 600,000-tonne structural supply deficit. The authors are explicitly bullish across the complex and contend that the convergence of geopolitical, fiscal and supply-side fundamentals cannot be durably overridden by one CPI print, however significant the short-term price damage.
